newsitem.title: USA: M. Stanley, Dean Witter deal lauded -- arbs.
newsitem.headline: M. Stanley, Dean Witter deal lauded -- arbs.

text.p: Morgan Stanley Group Inc and Dean Witter Discover & Co's surprise stock-swap merger was lauded by Wall Street arbitrageurs, who expect the deal to easily draw shareholder support and all necessary regulatory approvals.
"Although it is early, it is pretty clean deal. It makes a lot of sense and there are a lot of syneries," said an arb who declined to be identified.
He said the deal will need approval from all 50 state insurance commissioners, among other regulatory bodies, which is not expected to be a problem.

A second arb said, "It is amusing that Morgan Stanley actually got a premium and is retaining control, which is unusual in a deal. This will touch off a whole round of consolidation in the securities industry and there are no problems getting this deal done."
The first arb said, "They do not get effective control, they get half of the board, Morgan Stanley shareholders will own less 45 percent of the combined company," the second arb said.
In early New York Stock Exchange trade, Morgan Stanley shares soared 7-3/4 to 65-1/8 and Dean Witter shares added 1-3/4 to 40-3/8.
